known_facts_book1: King of the Nomes and Monarch of all the Metals and Precious Stones of the Underground World, seated on a throne of virgin gold in a jeweled cavern under a mountain.
Was formerly named Roquat; the book states outright that after he drank of the Waters of Oblivion he forgot his own name and had to take another.
A round little man with a flowing white beard, a red face, bright eyes and a scowl that covers all his forehead, wearing a crown cut from a single blood-red ruby.
Is surly and cross because mortals dug treasure out of the earth and kept it above ground, and hates both mortals and fairies.
Threw Tik-Tok down a well, and later dropped the whole party down the Forbidden Tube after having the path twisted toward it and the opening made invisible.
Had been warned repeatedly by Tititi-Hoochoo never to use the Tube, and did it anyway over Kaliko's protest.
Keeps a covered pit in the passage to trap invaders, a Magic Spyglass in the wall, and a great gong he beats to summon Kaliko.
Amuses himself by throwing his sceptre at Kaliko's head, and breaks the tip off the Long-Eared Hearer's ear by accident.
Transforms Shaggy into a dove and Ozga into a fiddle, and is about to transform Files into a fiddle bow when Quox interrupts.
Loses every magical power the instant he plainly looks at the pink ribbon around Quox's neck, which Tititi-Hoochoo enchanted for exactly that purpose.
Is driven from his kingdom not by force but by six hen's eggs rolled out of Quox's locket, which pursue him; nomes wither and blow away if the inside of an egg touches them.
Flees so fast that he forgets to fill his pockets, then has a poor woman sew pockets all over his robe and sneaks back through a secret passage into the Metal Forest.
Is captured there by the officers of Oogaboo, allowed by Kaliko to fill his pockets, and loses nearly all of it because the woman used poor thread and the pockets burst one by one along the passage.
Cannot remember how to break the charm of ugliness he cast on Shaggy's brother, beyond that it needs a certain kind of kiss.
Reforms at the end and is allowed by Kaliko to stay underground as a common nome, as long as he behaves — he is not left wandering the earth.

known_facts_book1: Ruggedo's High Chamberlain, the one nome intelligent and obedient enough that the King dares not mash him.
Is one of the nomes himself and as much abused as any; when the nomes throw down their hammers and picks, only Kaliko can get them working again.
Warns Ruggedo repeatedly not to use the Forbidden Tube and not to anger Tititi-Hoochoo, and is proved right on every count.
Writes himself letters of recommendation — honest man, good servant, small eater — expecting to need another job soon.
Kicks Tik-Tok's knee-joints from behind to bring him down, but then secretly hides Betsy and Hank in his own private room and feeds them mineral bread and broiled mushrooms.
Pleads with Ruggedo to spare Betsy, to release the Ugly One, and not to melt Tik-Tok — every time at risk to himself.
Is made King of the Nomes by Quox on the Jinjin's authority, because he believes he could rule no worse than Ruggedo and the nomes like him better.
Appoints Guph his Royal Chamberlain and promises not to throw the sceptre at his head unless he deserves it.
Does not know the way to the Metal Forest, since Ruggedo changed the location of its three secret passages every week.
Lets the deposed Ruggedo stay underground at Betsy's urging, on condition of good behavior.

known_facts_book1: Ruggedo's most famous General, who leads hundreds of nomes armed with sharp magic spears to the mouth of the Tube.
Waves his sword and calls the travelers down to be captured, then has his nomes hurl their spears — which rattle off Quox's silver scales and bound back into their owners' hands.
Is kicked into the Nome King by Hank's heels, flattening Ruggedo against the rock wall.
Tries repeatedly and fails to seize Polychrome, whose body is not where his hands close.
Flees with the other nomes when the six eggs roll out of Quox's locket, and bars the door in Ruggedo's face.
Is glad to be rid of so hard a master and is appointed Royal Chamberlain by King Kaliko.

known_facts_book1: A nome with enormous ears who can hear anything anywhere in the world, and who reports what he hears to the Nome King.
Spreads out his great ears and sways them to listen, and can judge distance to the furlong, foot and inch from the sound of voices.
Has one ear-tip broken off by Ruggedo's flung sceptre, which the King regrets because those ears are valuable to him.
Reports that Shaggy Man is coming to rescue his brother, and that the Army of Oogaboo means to take the King's metals and jewels.
Overhears Shaggy's plan to use the Love Magnet on Ruggedo, which is what makes the King have Shaggy bound before he can reach his pocket.
Cannot hear an egg, as Kaliko points out — only the Magic Spyglass can reveal those.

known_facts_book1: The leader of Ruggedo's score of executioners, nearly as evil looking as their master.
His nomes carry great golden pincers, silver prods, clamps, chains and other wicked-looking instruments, all of precious metals set with diamonds and rubies.
Is sent to fetch the Army of Oogaboo from the pit and finds them gone, then sent to the Slimy Cave and finds Betsy and Hank gone.
Reports that the prisoners 'left no address', and insists there is only one Slimy Cave.
Cuts the cords binding the dove's wings at Ruggedo's order after Shaggy is transformed.
Tortures nobody in the course of the book.
